knowledge:
- key_parameters: metric=The colData column name of the QC metric to evaluate in localOutliers ;; direction=The direction of outlier detection in localOutliers ("lower" or "higher") ;; log=Logical indicating whether to log-transform the metric in localOutliers (set to TRUE for sum/detected, FALSE for mitochondrial percentage) ;; mito_percent=The colData column name for mitochondrial percentage in findArtifacts ;; mito_sum=The colData column name for mitochondrial sum in findArtifacts ;; n_order=The neighborhood size/order (number of neighbors) to use for local variance calculation in findArtifacts ;; name=The colData column name where artifact detection results will be saved in findArtifacts ;; outliers=The colData column name indicating outlier status to highlight in plotQCmetrics
- alternatives: scuttle::addPerCellQCMetrics is used in the vignette for initial QC metric calculation, but the documentation notes it is deprecated in favor of scrapper::quickRnaQc.se or scrapper::computeRnaQcMetrics.
- when_to_use: Use during the preprocessing and quality control stage of spot-based spatial transcriptomics data analysis to detect spatially-correlated outliers and physical tissue artifacts (e.g., foldings, hangnails) that standard non-spatial QC methods fail to capture.
- pitfalls: localOutliers assumes a normal distribution, meaning library size (sum) and unique genes (detected) must be log-transformed (log = TRUE), whereas mitochondrial percentage should not be log-transformed (log = FALSE). Out-of-tissue spots must be removed from the SpatialExperiment object before running SpotSweeper functions to avoid confounding the local neighborhood calculations.

workflows.name: spot_level_local_outlier_detection
workflows.intent: Identify and visualize spatially-aware local outliers based on library size, unique genes, and mitochondrial percentage.
input: spe (SpatialExperiment object containing spot-based spatial transcriptomics data with spatial coordinates and in_tissue annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter out-of-tissue spots ;; 2. Calculate standard QC metrics (sum, detected, mitochondrial percentage) ;; 3. Run localOutliers for library size, unique genes, and mitochondrial percentage ;; 4. Combine individual outlier metrics into a single logical column ;; 5. Visualize the local outliers using plotQCmetrics
workflows.code:
library(SpotSweeper)

# load  Maynard et al DLPFC daatset
spe <- STexampleData::Visium_humanDLPFC()

# show column data before SpotSweeper
colnames(colData(spe))

# drop out-of-tissue spots
spe <- spe[, spe$in_tissue == 1]

# change from gene id to gene names
rownames(spe) <- rowData(spe)$gene_name

# identifying the mitochondrial transcripts
is.mito <- rownames(spe)[grepl("^MT-", rownames(spe))]

# calculating QC metrics for each spot using scuttle
spe <- scuttle::addPerCellQCMetrics(spe, subsets = list(Mito = is.mito))
colnames(colData(spe))

# library size
spe <- localOutliers(spe,
    metric = "sum",
    direction = "lower",
    log = TRUE
)

# unique genes
spe <- localOutliers(spe,
    metric = "detected",
    direction = "lower",
    log = TRUE
)

# mitochondrial percent
spe <- localOutliers(spe,
    metric = "subsets_Mito_percent",
    direction = "higher",
    log = FALSE
)

# combine all outliers into "local_outliers" column
spe$local_outliers <- as.logical(spe$sum_outliers) |
    as.logical(spe$detected_outliers) |
    as.logical(spe$subsets_Mito_percent_outliers)

library(escheR)

# all local outliers
plotQCmetrics(spe, metric = "sum_log", outliers = "local_outliers", point_size = 1.1, 
       stroke = 0.75) +
      ggtitle("All Local Outliers")

workflows.name: technical_artifact_detection
workflows.intent: Identify and visualize technical artifacts (such as tissue hangnails) using local variance of mitochondrial metrics across multiple neighborhood sizes.
input: spe (SpatialExperiment object containing spot-based spatial transcriptomics data with mitochondrial ratio and sum columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Visualize raw mitochondrial percentage to inspect for potential artifacts ;; 2. Run findArtifacts to cluster and identify technical artifacts ;; 3. Visualize the identified artifacts using plotQCmetrics
workflows.code:
# load in DLPFC sample with hangnail artifact
data(DLPFC_artifact)
spe <- DLPFC_artifact

# inspect colData before artifact detection
colnames(colData(spe))

plotQCmetrics(spe,
    metric = "expr_chrM_ratio",
    outliers = NULL, point_size = 1.1
) +
    ggtitle("Mitochondrial Percent")

# find artifacts using SpotSweeper
spe <- findArtifacts(spe,
    mito_percent = "expr_chrM_ratio",
    mito_sum = "expr_chrM",
    n_order = 5,
    name = "artifact"
)

# check that "artifact" is now in colData
colnames(colData(spe))

plotQCmetrics(spe,
    metric = "expr_chrM_ratio",
    outliers = "artifact", point_size = 1.1
) +
    ggtitle("Hangnail artifact")
